    Run an adaptive test live, one item at a time

    cat_start.Rd

    `cat_start()` creates a test session from a design, `cat_next()` returns the next item to administer, `cat_answer()` records a response and updates the trait estimate, and `cat_done()` says whether a stopping rule has been met. Sessions are ordinary R lists, so they can be stored between page loads of a web application (for example in 'shiny').

    Usage

    cat_start(design)

cat_next(session)

cat_answer(session, item, response)

cat_done(session)

    Arguments

    design

    A [cat_design()].

    session

    A session from `cat_start()` (or a previous `cat_answer()`).

    item

    Item name or index being answered.

    response

    The response, on the item's original score scale.

    Value

    `cat_start()` and `cat_answer()` return the updated session; `cat_next()` returns the name of the next item (or `NA` when the test is finished); `cat_done()` returns `TRUE`/`FALSE` with the reason as an attribute.

    Examples

    bank <- make_bank(b = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 40), a = 1.2, model = "2pl")
design <- cat_design(bank, max_items = 10)
s <- cat_start(design)
while (!cat_done(s)) {
  it <- cat_next(s)
  s <- cat_answer(s, it, response = rbinom(1, 1, 0.6))   # replace with a real answer
}
s
#> <cat_session> 10 item(s) administered | theta = -0.078, SE = 0.485 | finished: max_items
#>  step item response   theta    se
#>     1 I021        0 -0.4551 0.885
#>     2 I016        1 -0.0763 0.793
#>     3 I020        0 -0.3873 0.725
#>     4 I017        1 -0.1136 0.668
#>     5 I019        0 -0.3521 0.624
#>     6 I018        1 -0.1349 0.585
#>     7 I022        1  0.0786 0.557
#>     8 I023        0 -0.0740 0.528
#>     9 I024        0 -0.1915 0.506
#>    10 I015        1 -0.0784 0.485
